newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore April non-oil exports seen up 0.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Singapore April non-oil exports seen up 0.5 pct.

text.p: Singapore's non-oil domestic exports for April were likely to be modestly higher after five months of languishing in negative terrain, a Reuters poll of economists showed on Monday.
Eleven financial institutions surveyed produced an average 0.5 percent year-on-year forecast in nominal terms for non-oil exports, up from minus 2.1 percent in March.
This was the first positive read of the market after five consecutive months of negative growth from November.
Although the forecast was considered still flat, economists said this pointed to better prospects for the rest of the year.
The pullback in manufacturing, however, occured around May, when the base drifts lower. This should, therefore, result in stronger year-on-year growth numbers for the months ahead.
Electronics, which account for nearly 60 percent of exports, remain the main culprit for the setbacks to the economy, the economists said.
The consensus, however, was that a sharp jump in U.S. orders for semiconductors since early this year would begin to filter down to local producers in the second-half of 1997.
